category_title: Students requiring structured accountability during phonics dictation
minimal_context: The student is spelling and reading a list of words with the 'ook' pattern during a phonics dictation routine.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please write down the word 'cook' on your paper.

STUDENT: c - o - o - k

TUTOR: Okay. Now write down 'look', 'hook', and 'took'.

STUDENT: It's the ook family.

TUTOR: Yes. Now I want you to sit quietly and read that list of words by yourself over and over until time is up.

STUDENT: (Slides out of his chair and begins rolling on the floor instead of reading the list individually)

options.A: Provide the student with the option of changing to a different spelling or reading task at any time during the dictation routine.
options.B: Transform the solitary reading task into a supportive group effort, having students read the list together, then at a faster pace, then individually, then to a neighbor in rapid succession.
options.C: Deliberately avoid applying any pressure to the student during the reading task, including time pressure, performance pressure, or assessment pressure.
options.D: Terminate the reading demands immediately and remove the list of words and other materials from the student for 10 seconds.
